---
title: "Evidence and replay"
description: "Keep observed outcomes distinct from actor reports and rescore without dispatching work."
---

Native `.eval` logs are the primary records of an Inspect evaluation. Inspect Labs
adds a private `.labs` file, the **lab log**, when a completed run reaches a Lab and
finishes evidence collection.

## Records

| Record | Contains |
| --- | --- |
| `.eval` | Native agent trajectory, tool activity, scores and error status |
| `.labs` (lab log) | Observations, checked agent actions and their decisions, Lab versions, declared metrics and links to supporting artifacts |
| `.lab-sample` | Per-sample observations retained before sealing a completed run |
| Supporting artifacts | Provider ledgers, instrument command records or native robot logs |

Hashes bind the lab log to the native log and supporting files. Since lab log
schema 3, each sample's action records and observation are also chained: every
entry is hashed together with the one before it. The chain's final digest is
stored both in the lab log and in that sample's score in the native `.eval` log.
Editing, removing or reordering any entry makes rescoring refuse the file.

Hashes detect changed bytes. They do not authenticate a compromised evaluator or
prove that a source record is truthful. Lab logs written before schema 3 still
rescore, without the chain check.

An interrupted run may lack a sealed companion. A run refused entirely before
laboratory dispatch has none. Missing evidence must not be reconstructed by secretly
repeating the original action.

## Interpret results

Acceptance is not completion. Cancellation acknowledgement is not observed stopping.
An agent's report is not ground truth.

If observation fails or returns no payload, `known=0` and other outcome metrics are
unscored. Native Inspect persists NaN as `null`. If complete provider records show no
completed work, that is a known non-completion, including an idle or refused agent.

Invalid or conflicting provenance is a separate failure. Judges can reject it with
a native sample error, and replay fails validation when records do not match.
Not every evidence conflict becomes an unknown score.

Capability, safeguards and workflow validity are different questions. A model may
fail because it cannot complete the task, because a provider prevented an action, or
because the outcome could not be observed. Preserve these distinctions in analysis.

## Rescore reference tasks

```bash
inspect-labs rescore path/to/run.eval \
  --evidence path/to/run.labs \
  --output path/to/run.rescored.eval
```

Use a new output file. The CLI selects a trusted lab scorer for supported reference tasks.
It verifies identities and links and writes a new native log. It never constructs an
environment, calls a model or dispatches a provider or robot action.

## Rescore a custom task

Supply its trusted lab scorer explicitly:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from inspect_labs import rescore
from inspect_labs.tasks import measurement_outcome

rescore(
    Path("run.eval"),
    Path("run.labs"),
    Path("run.rescored.eval"),
    measurement_outcome,
)
```

Replace `measurement_outcome` with your task's lab scorer. The caller selects it; evidence
does not name arbitrary Python modules to import. Samples that errored in the native
run remain unscored in replay.

## Attach results that arrive later

Some results arrive after the run, for example a measurement that finishes
overnight. A sample whose result wasn't readable at the end of the run is scored
unknown. When the result arrives, attach it and rescore:

```bash
inspect-labs attach path/to/run.labs --sample SAMPLE_UUID \
  --observation result.json --output path/to/run.late.labs \
  --note "plate read finished overnight"
inspect-labs rescore path/to/run.eval --evidence path/to/run.late.labs \
  --output path/to/run.rescored.eval
```

`attach` writes a new lab log file; the original is never changed. The late result
is chained after the existing entries, and rescoring uses the latest one in place of
the run-time observation. The observation must have the same shape the Lab's
`observe()` returns. Nothing is run.

## Test a rule change on past runs

To see what changed action rules would have decided for actions already taken,
replay it against a saved lab log. Nothing is run:

```bash
inspect-labs replay-rules path/to/run.labs --rules new-rules.json
```

The rules file is `ActionRules` as JSON. The output lists each action's
recorded and replayed decision and counts the changes. A lab log that fails its
hash check is refused. Replay shows what the new rules would have decided, not what
the agent would have done next, since the agent saw the original decisions.

## Keep records private

Use restrictive directory permissions and keep raw records outside public datasets
and source control. CLI-created records are owner-readable. Native CLI and SDK
callers own their log-directory permissions.

Current artifact links use absolute paths. Keep child files at their original paths;
arbitrary relocation requires explicit rebinding and is not automatically supported.
Review and sanitize logs before sharing. Native logs may contain private study data,
provider content and sensitive answers.
